import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.55

by N. S. Chernikov

Is it true that a group which is a product of two almost abelian subgroups is
almost soluble?

Here a group is *almost abelian* (resp. *almost soluble*) if it has an abelian
(resp. soluble) subgroup of finite index, and a group $G$ is the *product* of
its subgroups $A$ and $B$ if $G = AB$, i.e. every element of $G$ can be written
as $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$. No finiteness assumption is made on $G$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.55»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is almost abelian (virtually abelian) if it has an abelian subgroup of
finite index. -/
def IsVirtuallyAbelian : Prop :=
  ∃ N : Subgroup G, IsMulCommutative N ∧ N.FiniteIndex

/-- A group $G$ is almost soluble (virtually soluble) if it has a soluble subgroup of
finite index. -/
def IsVirtuallySolvable : Prop :=
  ∃ N : Subgroup G, IsSolvable N ∧ N.FiniteIndex

variable {G}

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsMulCommutative.isVirtuallyAbelian [IsMulCommutative G] : IsVirtuallyAbelian G :=
  ⟨⊤, inferInstance, inferInstance⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsSolvable.isVirtuallySolvable [IsSolvable G] : IsVirtuallySolvable G :=
  ⟨⊤, inferInstance, inferInstance⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsVirtuallyAbelian.isVirtuallySolvable (h : IsVirtuallyAbelian G) :
    IsVirtuallySolvable G := by
  obtain ⟨N, hN, hfin⟩ := h
  exact ⟨N, inferInstance, hfin⟩

/--
Is it true that a group which is a product of two almost abelian subgroups is
almost soluble?

That is, if $G = AB$ for subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ (every $g \in G$ is of the form
$ab$ with $a \in A$, $b \in B$) and both $A$ and $B$ are almost abelian, must $G$ be
almost soluble?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G),
      IsVirtuallyAbelian A → IsVirtuallyAbelian B →
      (∀ g : G, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, a * b = g) →
      IsVirtuallySolvable G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.55»

    IsVirtuallyAbelian G :=

  ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance⟩

  obtain ⟨A, hA, hfin⟩ := h
  exact ⟨A, isSolvable_of_comm fun a b => mul_comm a b, hfin⟩

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.55

by N. S. Chernikov

Is it true that a group which is a product of two almost abelian subgroups is
almost soluble?

Here a group is *almost abelian* (virtually abelian) if it has an abelian
subgroup of finite index, and *almost soluble* (virtually soluble) if it has a
soluble subgroup of finite index. A group $G$ is the *product* of two subgroups
$A$ and $B$ if $G = AB$, i.e. every element of $G$ can be written as $ab$ with
$a \in A$ and $b \in B$. No finiteness assumption is made on $G$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«7.55»

/-- A group is *almost abelian* (virtually abelian) if it has an abelian subgroup
of finite index. -/
def IsVirtuallyAbelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ H : Subgroup G, H.FiniteIndex ∧ IsMulCommutative H

/-- A group is *almost soluble* (virtually soluble) if it has a soluble subgroup
of finite index. -/
def IsVirtuallySolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ H : Subgroup G, H.FiniteIndex ∧ IsSolvable H

/-- An abelian group is almost abelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isVirtuallyAbelian_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsVirtuallyAbelian G :=
  ⟨⊤, inferInstance, inferInstance⟩

/-- An almost abelian group is almost soluble. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsVirtuallyAbelian.isVirtuallySolvable {G : Type*} [Group G]
    (hG : IsVirtuallyAbelian G) : IsVirtuallySolvable G := by
  obtain ⟨H, hH, _⟩ := hG
  exact ⟨H, hH, inferInstance⟩

/-- A finite group is almost soluble. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isVirtuallySolvable_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsVirtuallySolvable G :=
  ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance⟩

/--
Is it true that a group which is a product of two almost abelian subgroups is
almost soluble?

That is, for every group $G$ and subgroups $A, B \leq G$ with $G = AB$, if $A$ and
$B$ are almost abelian (each has an abelian subgroup of finite index), must $G$ be
almost soluble (have a soluble subgroup of finite index)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G),
      IsVirtuallyAbelian A → IsVirtuallyAbelian B →
      (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ →
      IsVirtuallySolvable G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.55»
